The edges that matter most, per sd, all lower the predicted probability of earning at most 50K as the input rises: education-num -0.879, married to a civilian spouse -0.691, husband -0.622, wife -0.516, male sex -0.342, capital loss -0.264 and hours per week -0.301. In the whole model, the typical case gets 64% at education 9 and 31% at education 13 on the 1-16 scale; 74%, 64% and 52% at 20, 40 and 60 hours a week; 78% as a woman against 64% as a man; 32% with a capital loss of 2,000 dollars; and 88% if never married against 64% married to a civilian spouse. One edge is fitted to a tiny group: workclass:8 (without pay) has weight 1.05 per sd and adds 50.3 to the logit on the 17 without-pay training rows, whose mean predicted probability is 1.0000 (fitted to 17 rows, outcome rate 88%). Switching the direct terms off to their mean lowers the training AUC from 0.913 to 0.677, the largest loss of any part.
ann_124.proposed: Each input's own contribution, added up one input at a time: more education, capital losses and working hours lower the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less); being a woman, not being a husband and some rare countries of birth raise it.

ann_125.original: The model adds the logit contributions of its twelve parts at the output node and passes the sum through a sigmoid to give the predicted probability of earning at most 50K (training outcome rate 76%, training AUC 0.913). The parts meet at the output node, where their contributions are summed, so their effects add on the logit scale: in the typical case the score is 0.560; age 25 moves it to 1.732, a capital gain of 8,000 dollars to -3.179, and both together to -2.008, which is the sum of the two separate changes. The interactions the model has sit inside parts: capital gain with not-in-family relationship (capital_gain_switch) and handlers or cleaners with Asian or Pacific Islander race (handlers_asian_gate). The three largest parts by single-part ablation are the direct terms (training AUC 0.913 with them, 0.677 switched off), the capital-gain switch (0.891 switched off) and the young-age hinge (0.905 switched off); the handlers and Asian gate is next (0.9121). Two terms are fitted to tiny groups and push them to near-certain predictions: the Scotland gate and edge (16 rows) and the without-pay edge (17 rows).
ann_125.proposed: The model adds up separate contributions from its parts; capital gains and education level move the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) by large amounts (for the typical person, from about 64% to about 12% as capital gains go from 0 US dollars to 6849 US dollars).

parts.original_hypothesis: The model adds the logit contributions of its twelve parts at the output node and passes the sum through a sigmoid to give the predicted probability of earning at most 50K (training outcome rate 76%, training AUC 0.913). The interactions the model has sit inside parts: capital gain with not-in-family relationship (capital_gain_switch) and handlers or cleaners with Asian or Pacific Islander race (handlers_asian_gate). The three largest parts by single-part ablation are the direct terms (training AUC 0.913 with them, 0.677 switched off), the capital-gain switch (0.891 switched off) and the young-age hinge (0.905 switched off); the handlers and Asian gate is next (0.9121). Two terms are fitted to tiny groups and push them to near-certain predictions: the Scotland gate and edge (16 rows) and the without-pay edge (17 rows).

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient); an input the data ties to a category takes its typical value within that category (linked inputs)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients
